name: Monfalcone
title: Monfalcone Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging | Bulk & Project Cargo
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement at Monfalcone for bulk carriers, steel and paper ships and project cargo vessels: hold, hatch cover and ballast tank gauging.
h1: Hold and Hull Gauging for Bulk and Steel Ships at Monfalcone
intro: Monfalcone sits at the northern tip of the Adriatic, where the Gulf of Trieste narrows towards the Isonzo plain. It is a shipbuilding town with a commercial port beside the yard, and the ships that call here carry steel, paper, bulk and heavy project cargo. They tend to be mid-sized and hard-worked, and their holds see a lot of abuse. Our technicians travel from India to the ship at the quay.

highlights.p: Steel coils, plate and slabs hit tank tops, hold frames and lower hopper plating hard during loading. Gauging the damaged and corroded strakes after discharge shows what the next cargo will face.
Paper and steel cargoes need dry holds, so hatch cover panels and coaming plating matter. We measure panel plating, stiffeners and coamings, with magnetic particle testing at cracks near cleats.
Water is shallow in the northern gulf, and ships here are limited in draught. Berth, tide and cargo timing decide the working window, which we agree with the agent before the team travels.

port.h: A working port in the Gulf of Trieste
p: The port of Monfalcone lies on the northeastern shore of the Gulf of Trieste, close to the mouth of the Isonzo and the border with Slovenia. It is a short distance north-west of Trieste along the coast road, and administratively it belongs to the same eastern Adriatic port system. The water is shallow compared with Trieste's deep terminals, and a dredged approach channel keeps the commercial quays open to mid-sized ships, with draught and length limits that exclude the largest bulkers.

Monfalcone's identity is industrial. A large shipyard dominates the waterfront and builds big passenger ships, so the port is also a supplier of project cargo and steel for the yard. Ships bring steel plate and coils, forest products, paper, general cargo, bulk materials and heavy lifts. The commercial quays handle dry bulk and break-bulk, and some berths are used for vehicle cargoes or for ships waiting to load. Traffic is steady and unglamorous, which suits the repeat voyages of mid-sized ships on short Mediterranean routes.

The northern Adriatic has its own weather. The bora, a cold, strong wind from the north-east, can blow hard in winter, closing berths and halting loading, while summers are calmer with occasional thunderstorms. Fog and shallow water also play a part in the cold months. Ships waiting for a berth anchor in the gulf off Trieste or Monfalcone, but anchorage work depends on the bora being absent. For gauging the realistic windows are quay calls with the holds empty and cleaned. Owners who plan around the winter wind often schedule heavier scopes for the calmer spring and autumn weeks, when berths run to time and launch transfers are dependable.

facilities.h: Quays, the shipyard neighbour and the nearest dock
p: The commercial quays are the main place for gauging at Monfalcone. Bulk and general cargo ships lie alongside while cargo is discharged or loaded, and the holds are empty for short periods between operations. Hold frames, tank tops, lower hopper plating and hatch coamings can then be measured with the ship's staging or a scissor lift, provided the holds are swept and the terminal agrees to the access. The adjacent shipyard is a newbuilding yard, not a repair yard, so owners do not normally dock merchant ships there.

When a docking or a renewal survey is due, ships typically move to a repair yard elsewhere on the Adriatic, in Croatia, or further afield in the Mediterranean, and the Monfalcone readings go with the ship as a baseline. For a ship waiting for berth, the anchorage in the gulf is open to the bora, so pre-docking work there is weather dependent. In all cases the agent submits the team's details to the port authority and the terminal security staff well before the ship arrives.
list: Commercial quays: hold frames, tank tops and lower hopper plating on bulk and steel carriers after discharge.
Steel and project cargo berths: hatch cover, coaming and deck gauging on ships carrying coils, plate and heavy lifts.
Forest products and paper berths: hold and hatch cover gauging on ships that need weathertight holds.
Quay frontage for general cargo ships: ballast tank and deck readings between cargo operations.
Anchorage in the Gulf of Trieste: launch-served condition gauging when the weather and the agent allow.
Handover to a repair yard: readings prepared in TM plan format for a docking elsewhere in the Adriatic.

context.h: Italian coast guard rules and the Adriatic trade
p: Ships calling at Monfalcone fall under Italian port state control, carried out by the Coast Guard, and the Paris MoU inspection regime applies. The harbour office responsible for the area controls berthing, cargo and safety matters, and its approval is needed for work involving hot work or tank entry on ships alongside. Steel carriers and older general cargo ships are exactly the type that attracts the attention of port state control, because of hold structure, hatch covers and weathertight integrity.

The trade itself drives the need for gauging. Steel cargoes are heavy, and loading with grabs and cranes damages tank tops and frames. Older mid-sized ships working from this part of the Adriatic are often in their later survey cycles, where owners consider each docking carefully. Gauging in Monfalcone helps the owner decide whether a renewal can wait for the next season. Under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, owners also keep an eye on the Inventory of Hazardous Materials for ships heading toward the end of their trading life.

jobs.p: Jobs at Monfalcone usually start with a cargo ship that has taken punishment from steel or bulk loading and needs an honest view of the steel before the next survey. The superintendent defines the holds and tanks, the agent confirms the discharge and cleaning schedule, and the team measures once the spaces are safe. Results go to the owner and, where relevant, to the repair yard. Typical requests are:
list: A steel coil carrier after discharge: tank top, hold frames and lower hopper plate gauging, with magnetic particle testing at frame brackets.
A bulk carrier at the quay: hatch cover panel, coaming and topside tank readings ahead of an intermediate survey.
A paper carrier: hold boundary and hatch cover gauging, aimed at weathertight integrity before the next loading.
A general cargo ship on a project charter: deck, crane pedestal and ballast tank gauging before heavy cargo is loaded.
A pre-purchase check on a mid-sized cargo ship lying at the quay, completed in a day or two.

logistics: Trieste Airport at Ronchi dei Legionari lies close to Monfalcone, and Venice Marco Polo is the larger alternative with a longer road transfer, so the team can reach the port easily by road. Technicians from India need a Schengen visa for Italy, applied for after the ship's call is confirmed. Port access and terminal security passes are requested through the ship's agent, with the team's passport and certificate details supplied in advance.

faqs.q: When can the holds be gauged at Monfalcone?
faqs.a: After discharge, once the holds are swept and the terminal allows access. On steel ships the window can be short, because loading starts soon after discharge ends. We agree a priority list with the superintendent so the most damaged strakes are measured first.

faqs.q: Is there a repair drydock at Monfalcone?
faqs.a: The shipyard here builds passenger ships and does not normally dock merchant ships for repair. Ships that need a docking go to yards elsewhere on the Adriatic or in the wider Mediterranean, and the Monfalcone readings travel with them.

faqs.q: Does the bora stop work in the port?
faqs.a: It can. Strong north-easterly wind may halt loading, close berths and make anchorage transfers unsafe. Quay work inside the holds is less affected than anchorage jobs, but we keep a flexible date with the superintendent during the winter months.

faqs.q: Can hatch covers be checked while the ship is loading?
faqs.a: Only on covers that are open and safe to reach, and only where the terminal and ship agree. More often the best moment is after discharge, with hatches open and decks clear. We measure panel plating and coamings and use magnetic particle testing at suspect welds.
